content.comment_body: During online testing, the text appears correctly on the PC screen, but not on the [product_name] device and TD display. An odd issue is that the text block numbers start from 16. When creating a new program, text block numbers begin at 1 and the text is properly shown on the display. See the attachment for reference. Thank you in advance. [user_name]

Hello [user_name], I'm not experienced with [product_name], but I'll try to help. Why did you enable Character Set 2 ISO_8859_1 in SF016? (This function currently has high priority for you.) You might need to disable this setting and test again. The numbering of SF depends on whether you used other special functions earlier to insert message blocks. Hope this helps. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, I don't think the second character set is the issue, since it would require activating with flag M27, similar to a shift function, which isn’t done here. If you add messages again (the block numbers are automatically assigned starting from the first function (B001), then the second (B002), and so on), the priority also increases starting from priority 0. Example: SF016 now has priority 10 (high). If you place it again in a blank circuit, it will be SF001 with priority 0 (low). Each additional message will have a higher priority. If you want to adjust this, check the settings for each message text. So I suggest reviewing the priority for every message again. I hope this explanation is clear.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing inconsistencies between text displayed during PC simulation and on the actual [product_name] device and TD display. The issue appears to be related to text block numbering, which sometimes starts at 16 instead of 1, causing messages not to show on the physical device. There is also confusion around message priority settings and character set configuration, leading to additional challenges in managing and displaying message texts properly.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect message texts to appear consistently on both PC simulation and the [product_name] display, regardless of block numbering. They desire straightforward management of message blocks and reliable text output on hardware.
